question: A gift shop had 39 items. They multiplied by 9 through a new shipment. Then added 61 more items from a vendor. The collection multiplied by 9 again for a store expansion. Finally, 72 items were added as opening inventory. A pop-up shop 5 miles away had 150 items but separate location. How many total items are in the expanded store?

A shop had 155 items. They added 69 more through restocking. The inventory multiplied by 7 for a holiday sale prep. Then 67 items were removed for display cases. All items were divided by 5 to show distribution to 5 departments. A boutique store had 100 items but independent operations. How many items does each department receive?

A team started with 146 members. They multiplied by 6, then by 4 again through consecutive recruiting drives. They added 14 more from a final round. Then 43 volunteers joined. Finally, 56 additional members signed up. A sister organization had 500 members but separate roster. How many total members does the team have now?

A group started with 148 participants. In the morning, 35 dropped out. The remainder multiplied by 6 for afternoon shifts. Then they multiplied by 2 more for evening teams. The evening total multiplied by 9 for capacity planning. Finally, they multiplied by 2 again for future sessions. A sister program had 300 participants but independent planning. How many participant slots are planned for future capacity?

A student scored 169 points to start. They multiplied by 6 through bonus questions. Then 14 points were added from extra credit. The total multiplied by 7 for weighting. Finally, they multiplied by 3 again for final calculation. Their lab partner scored 150 points independently. How many weighted points is the final score?

Maria started with 100 dollars in her savings account. She doubled her money by picking up extra shifts at work. Then she spent 165 dollars on car repairs. She earned 48 dollars from selling old textbooks, received 59 dollars from her parents, and found 31 dollars in an old jacket pocket. How much money did Maria have at the end, in dollars?

A bookshelf had 179 books initially. James removed 20 books to donate. He bought 49 more books during a sale. He then organized the books into 4 equal piles and took one pile home. He added 26 books to his collection. He then multiplied his collection by 4 when he started a library. Finally, he removed 294 books that were damaged. How many books did James have after all these changes?

Tom started with 156 dollars. He multiplied his money by 9 when he received his paycheck bonus. He then added 37 dollars from a refund. He received another 18 dollars from a friend. He got 30 dollars as a birthday gift. Finally, he spent 152 dollars on electronics. How much money did Tom have at the end?

A bakery had 225 cookies. In the morning, they baked 43 more cookies. They multiplied their stock by 5 for a party order. By afternoon, they sold 249 cookies to customers. In the evening, they multiplied their remaining stock by 5 for bulk storage. The bakery had a delivery truck (12 cookies, not used). How many cookies did the bakery have at closing time?

Sarah started with 41 songs on her playlist. She added 21 songs in the morning. She added 60 more songs in the afternoon. She removed 36 songs that were too long. She removed another 67 songs she didn't like anymore. She doubled her playlist size. How many songs did Sarah's playlist contain at the end?

A recipe called for 60 millilitres of oil. Sarah multiplied the amount by 3 to make enough for a family gathering. She added 25 more millilitres for extra cooking. She removed 45 millilitres for another dish. She removed 62 more millilitres by mistake. How much oil did she have left in millilitres?

A store had 216 pairs of shoes. They multiplied inventory by 5 after a big order. They added 21 pairs from a new shipment. They divided the stock by 3 for three warehouse locations. They removed 95 pairs that were sold. They divided again by 4 to prepare for a new season. They multiplied by 9 for the final display count. How many pairs of shoes were on display?

A warehouse started with 180 boxes. They removed 149 boxes for shipment. They added 72 boxes from a new delivery. They multiplied remaining stock by 6 for the inventory count. They added 10 more boxes from lost and found. They multiplied again by 6. They removed 3138 boxes for a bulk order. How many boxes remained?

A garden started with 63 plants. They multiplied the count by 7 after spring growth. They removed 322 plants during a renovation. They removed another 94 plants that died. They added 77 new plants from a nursery. They added 53 more flowering plants. They added 63 vegetable seedlings. How many plants were in the final garden?

A jeweler had 80 pieces of jewelry. He added 77 new designs. He removed 146 pieces for a sale. He added 14 pieces from a consignment. He added 10 pieces as trades from customers. He added 38 pieces from a local artisan. How many pieces did the jeweler have?

A photographer started with 204 photos. He added 7 photos from the morning shoot. He added 78 more photos from the afternoon session. He multiplied his collection by 5 for backup folders. He added 11 photos from evening captures. He added 55 more photos from client deliverables. He had 50 blurry photos (not counted). How many final photos did he have?

A student started with 130 dollars for supplies. She removed 99 dollars on textbooks. She added 53 dollars from a part-time job. She multiplied by 4 to plan her semester budget. She added 50 dollars from savings. She added 38 dollars from a gift. She found a 15-dollar coupon (not applied). What was her final budget amount?

A shop had 205 items. In the morning, they removed 46 items for a flash sale. By afternoon, they added 17 items from returns. By evening, they added 26 new items to inventory. They multiplied the display by 6 for a weekend showcase. Emma had 8 items in the storage room and David had 12 items. How many items were in the final display?

A factory started with 88 gadgets. They added 7 gadgets from early morning production. They removed 60 gadgets for quality control. They multiplied by 8 for the hourly forecast. They divided by 5 for five production lines. They multiplied by 4 for staffing calculation. They removed 102 defective gadgets. How many good gadgets remained?

A library's inventory was 202 reference materials. They removed 92 items for archiving. They removed 68 more items for digitization. They added 72 new materials from a purchase order. They added 12 items from donations. They removed 18 items that were lost. How many reference materials did the library have?

A tech company started the morning with 213 software patches. They multiplied workload by 9 for deployment. They added 26 patches from new bug reports. They multiplied the total by 3 for all servers. They removed 1322 patches from old systems. They removed another 3738 patches during cleanup. How many patches remained in the system?

A factory produced 175 units. They removed 126 units for export. They multiplied remaining units by 3 for domestic stock. They added 8 units from the workshop. They removed 22 units for quality checks. They multiplied by 8 for annual production planning. They multiplied by 4 for the forecast period. How many units were projected?

A garden had 50 tomato plants. They multiplied by 5 for spring planting. They added 69 plants from the nursery. They multiplied by 3 for the total garden expansion. They removed 578 plants for a market sale. They removed another 14 plants that wilted. What was the final count of tomato plants?

A bakery started with 201 loaves of bread. They added 75 loaves from the morning oven. They multiplied by 8 for the daily stock. They multiplied by 7 for weekly production. They added 55 more loaves from the second bakery. They tripled for the monthly forecast. How many loaves were needed for inventory?

A library had 205 books to catalog. They added 18 books from a donation. They added 65 more books from returns. They doubled for the backup copy system. They removed 315 books that were withdrawn. They added 25 books from a new purchase. How many books were in the final catalog?
